title: Weekly Markets Monitor - Golden Week in China
gist: World Gold Council's weekly monitor teaser: geopolitics dominated (US-China truce extended two months, US-Iran stalemate keeps energy and inflation elevated), and China's Golden Week may release postponed jewellery demand after a weak 2026 hurt by high prices and low confidence. Full data is in the downloadable PDF, not the page text.

insights.claim: China's Golden Week (1-7 October, National Day holiday) usually marks the start of the peak gold buying season, bringing stronger jewellery sales, trade restocking and firmer local premiums.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Watch the Shanghai premium over LBMA in early October as a real-time read on Chinese physical demand.

insights.claim: Elevated gold prices and low consumer confidence, among other factors, have dented China's gold jewellery demand so far in 2026.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Chinese jewellery demand is price-elastic and has been a drag in 2026, tempering the physical-demand bull case.

insights.claim: Recent gold price stability plus holiday spending may unlock postponed Chinese jewellery demand and give seasonal support into year end, as the historical pattern suggests.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Stable prices rather than falling ones can be the trigger for pent-up Chinese buying; a price spike would undermine it.

insights.claim: The chart of the week tracks the Chinese gold price premium using weekly average Au9999 (Shanghai Gold Exchange) versus the LBMA Gold Price PM as of 25 September 2026.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: The Au9999 vs LBMA spread is the gauge to monitor for Chinese demand strength.

insights.claim: The Trump-Xi summit produced a two-month extension of the US-China trade truce.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: A truce extension lowers near-term tariff escalation risk but only defers it by two months.

insights.claim: The stalemate in the US-Iran conflict persisted, keeping energy prices elevated and inflation concerns in focus.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Persistent oil-driven inflation worries affect rate expectations and gold's macro drivers.

insights.claim: Business activity strengthened in the US, Eurozone and India but softened in Japan and the UK, while US labor markets continued to show strength.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Divergent PMIs with a firm US labor market argue against aggressive near-term easing.

insights.claim: Major global equities ended the week higher while bond yields climbed, the US dollar strengthened and oil stayed elevated.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Rising yields and a stronger dollar are typical headwinds for gold in the short run.
